title: Valorization of  Casimiroa edulis  seed biowaste into magnetic biochar for efficient removal of ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin from wastewater
content: The discharge of pharmaceutical wastewater containing antibiotic residues poses a significant environmental concern. In this study, a magnetic biochar composite derived from Casimiroa edulis seed biowaste (Fe3O4–CSBC) was synthesized by in situ co-precipitation for the adsorptive removal of ciprofloxacin (CIP) and norfloxacin (NOR) from wastewater. The composite was characterized by FTIR, BET, XRD, TGA, SEM-EDS, and XPS to investigate its surface functional groups, textural properties, crystalline structure, thermal stability, morphology, elemental composition, and surface chemical states. Under optimized conditions, removal efficiencies of 95% for CIP and 93% for NOR were achieved at a contact time of 40 min, an adsorbent dosage of 0.3 g L−1, and pH values of 6.5 and 7.0 for CIP and NOR, respectively. The maximum adsorption capacities estimated using the nonlinear Langmuir model were 80.78 ± 2.4 mg g−1 for CIP and 74.74 ± 2.67 mg g−1 for NOR. However, the equilibrium data were better described by the Redlich–Peterson and Sips models, suggesting that adsorption occurred on a heterogeneous surface. The strong fits of the pseudo-second-order (PSO) and Elovich kinetic models, together with adsorption-induced FTIR band shifts and the negative enthalpy changes, were consistent with substantial adsorbate–surface interactions and a possible contribution from chemisorption-related processes. Thermodynamic analysis indicated that adsorption was spontaneous and exothermic under the investigated conditions. In real pharmaceutical wastewater, CIP and NOR concentrations decreased from 6.75 and 5.45 mg L−1 to 0.765 and 0.68 mg L−1, respectively. After five adsorption–desorption cycles, the composite retained removal efficiencies of 89.56% for CIP and 87.94% for NOR. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of Fe3O4–CSBC as a reusable, magnetically recoverable adsorbent for removing CIP and NOR from wastewater.
